title: Give the issuer only the time the ATM still waits

blocks.text: An acquirer's ATMs wait 15 seconds for the answer to a withdrawal, then show "unable to process" and send a reversal. On payday evenings the server's queue and its PIN checks are slow, and the issuer's team reports approvals for withdrawals that were reversed a few seconds later, and requests for withdrawals whose ATM had already given up. Each one holds the cardholder's money until the reversal arrives.

`AskIssuer`, in `src/main/java/com/example/practice/AskIssuer.java`, asks the issuer about each withdrawal and leaves the answer for the participant after it. Its `terminal-wait` property is how long the ATMs wait. Finish `remaining` and `ask`, marked `TODO`: the issuer must never be given longer than the ATM is still waiting, and a withdrawal its ATM has stopped waiting for must not reach the issuer at all. Then the transaction stops, and its `Result` says why, so the participant that answers on the abort path has a cause. About ten lines in total.
The tests call `prepare` the way the TransactionManager does, with a Context like the one `IncomingListener` builds, and an issuer link registered as a MUX that records what it was sent.

cases.says: a withdrawal that has just arrived is sent to the issuer and its answer is left in the Context
the issuer's timeout is the ATM's wait minus the time since the withdrawal arrived, not the whole wait
a withdrawal older than the ATM's wait is not sent at all; the transaction stops with a reported cause

origin.section: 13.2.1 The 2.1.7 Way to a Deadline: Compare the Arrival Time With the Clock

concepts: On 2.1.7 a deadline is measured from the TIMESTAMP IncomingListener stores on arrival, so queue time counts, and work the terminal no longer waits for is not done.
